about.en: A partner who pulls the foot back from the minor inner reap leans forward to balance. Turning in and sweeping the thigh from between the legs takes them over in the direction of the lean.

en: Reap at their right heel from the inside with Ko-uchi-gari.
Feel them pull the foot back out of the sweep, leaning forward as they take it away.
Keep the sleeve and lapel drawing them onto you so the lean becomes a forward off-balance.
Step your right foot between their feet, pivot, and swing your left foot round so your back turns into their chest.
Sweep your right leg backwards and upwards between their legs, against the inside of their left thigh, while your head and chest drive down and round to the left.
They come over your hip and sweeping leg and land ahead of you. Stay on the supporting leg and keep the sleeve.

receiving.en: Taking the foot back off a minor inner reap is the right move and it tips you forward onto the thrower, which is where the inner thigh throw begins. The second attack comes in the direction you were already leaning, so it arrives faster than the first. Do not straighten up into it; follow the rotation, keep your chin on your chest, and slap hard as your back lands. Recovering your posture with the foot is what breaks the pair.

viNotes.en: Both attacks are read through the grips: the foot coming back and the weight arriving forward are one signal. Turn in on that signal without pausing, since the opening closes as soon as they get their hips back. Your supporting leg between their feet and their thigh against yours are the two contacts that tell you the sweep is in place.
